subject: NewtonGate private deploy - MTU asymmetry causing SNAT resets
messages:
From: Alex Kerr <alex.kerr@newtongate.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent large-upload failures from on-prem to Private v1 (NewtonGate)

Hi team,

We're seeing repeated failures when NewtonGate customers upload artifacts > ~1MB to our Private deployment (customer VPC -> Redwood Private front-door). Symptoms: transfers start, then get a flurry of TCP RSTs and the client reports "connection reset by peer". This has been occurring intermittently for ~4 hours across two datacenters in their DC1 region.

What we've captured so far:
- Client side: curl PUTs to https://private.newtongate.example/upload fail ~20-30% of the time.
- tcpdump on their edge shows MSS advertised 1460, then we see duplicated packets/drop and quick RSTs.
- traceroute from client -> our private front-door shows an MTU mismatch (ICMP Fragmentation Needed) at a transit hop (AS64512) for frames >1500.
- In some traces the NAT translation differs mid-flow (different source port / outside IP), which suggests provider-side ECMP + NAT behavior.

I attached the initial netlogs bundle and a short pcap. Can Redwood help validate whether this looks like an MTU blackhole vs a SNAT/session-table churn on your side? We'd like to rule out any Redwood config that might be flipping SNAT or removing state.

Attachments: newtongate_netlogs.tar.gz (logs + iperf), client_pcap_01.pcap (20 packets around failure)

Urgency: high — affecting multiple customers and blocking artifact pushing in CI.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Kerr | NewtonGate SRE
alex.kerr@newtongate.com

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Kerr <alex.kerr@newtongate.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent large-upload failures from on-prem to Private v1 (NewtonGate)

Thanks Alex — and thanks for the logs. I pulled the bundle and started a quick triage. Key observations so far:

- I can reproduce an upload failure from our staging environment when I force path MTU >1500 to one of NewtonGate's test prefixes. The pcap shows "ICMP Fragmentation Needed" followed by retransmits and a short burst of RSTs.
- In multiple client pcaps I see alternating source addresses/ports for what looks like the same TCP flow — that strongly suggests asymmetric NAT/ECMP behavior in the transit provider.

Immediate ask from us to help accelerate:
- Can NewtonGate run a short tcpdump on the edge while we attempt an instrumented upload (I'd like IP/port + outer/inner IPs included)?
- Please run /proc/sys/net/ipv4/netfilter/ip_conntrack_count (or conntrack -L) around a failing upload and share output.
- If you can temporarily clamp MTU on the client-facing VLAN to 1400 for a single host (safely, during a test window) we can test if the failures stop.

Proposed short-term mitigations we'll try on our side:
- Ensure our Private front-door is not doing any mid-flow SNAT rotation; I've asked infra to audit the SNAT pool configuration for the affected route.
- Add an on-path MTU clamp on the egress host in staging to test compatibility.

We'll escalate if the above reproduces. Can you prioritize a 30-60m maintenance window today or tomorrow morning so we can run an instrumented test with tcpdump + conntrack dumps?

From: Alex Kerr <alex.kerr@newtongate.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent large-upload failures from on-prem to Private v1 (NewtonGate)

Connor — thanks for the quick reply.

We ran the conntrack snapshot during a failed upload and attached a filtered conntrack dump (included in the new netlogs bundle). A few notes from our side:
- The transit provider confirmed they have ECMP + asymmetric egress NAT on the path; they said this is by design for the affected pop.
- In the conntrack dump we can see entries timing out and a small window where outbound packets are using a different provider SNAT address.
- When we forced MTU clamp to 1400 on the client host the uploads completed successfully for a series of attempts (10/10).

We opened a ticket with the transit provider (ticket #TP-9981) and shared the pcap excerpt. They're looking into NAT behavior but warned it may take a day.

Immediate asks back to Redwood:
- Can you confirm whether your Private front-door does any source IP/port re-write for sessions coming from NewtonGate prefixes?
- If the front-door is stateless in that path, we're inclined to recommend Redwood raise a high-priority connectivity ticket with the provider to request sticky SNAT or avoid ECMP for this customer route.

Attachments: client_pcap_01.pcap (filtered), newton_conntrack_snapshot.txt

Alex

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Alex Kerr <alex.kerr@newtongate.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent large-upload failures from on-prem to Private v1 (NewtonGate)

Looping in an action plan and next steps. I'm marking this as a P1 connectivity escalation to get coordinated with provider ops.

Action items (Redwood):
- Infra (Connor + Karthik): audit SNAT pool behavior for the affected private endpoint and confirm whether any mid-flow SNAT rotation is possible. Share config snippets by EOD.
- Prod Networking (Grace): open a formal connectivity case with the transit provider (TP-9981) and request either sticky SNAT or per-flow pinning on the problematic POP. Provide them the pcap/conntrack evidence.
- Customer coordination (Connor): schedule a 60m maintenance window with NewtonGate for Monday 2027-06-07 08:30-09:30 PT to run a controlled test (we will attempt MTU clamp + staged upload).

Short-term mitigation: if provider cannot change behavior quickly, we should support customer with either:
- A recommended MTU clamp on their edge for affected builds (documented in the attached playbook), or
- A temporary dedicated route with provider that disables ECMP for the prefix (longer lead time).

I attached the current private-connectivity playbook with a checklist for triage and the SNAT audit commands. Please update the playbook with any additional items you run.

Attachments: redwood_private_playbook_v1.pdf

Thanks all — keep updates in thread and create NET-4321 ticket once the provider case is open.

Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
